conviction_note: The findings sum to +0.8. Peers that spoke after CMC (STLD on 09-17) describe wider metal margins and lower scrap through September, and US rebar ($1,022/t in August) and scrap (flat) say the Jun-Aug quarter landed inside CMC's own guide for a sequential core EBITDA increase of +$40-50m. Against that: both NUE and STLD guided below sell-side consensus, CMC has sold four of its last five prints on day 0, and the Q1 FY27 guide (seasonal, with West Virginia start-up) is the unknown line. So p_up is only 52 on a 5.0% absolute move, giving a scaled +0.2. The scaled number is a quarter of the findings sum because the sum is mostly small reads of the quarter that the company already guided to.
bar: FQ4 FY26 adjusted EPS consensus about $1.94-$2.00: Chartmill $1.94 / rev $2.55bn (https://www.chartmill.com/news/CMC/Chartmill-50275-Commercial-Metals-Co-NYSECMC-Delivers-Revenue-Beat-but-Earnings-Miss-Sinks-Stock), Earnings Whispers $1.97 / rev $2.45bn (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CMC), Benzinga $2.00 / rev $2.54bn (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CMC/earnings-forecasts), webull preview $1.98 / rev $2.56bn (https://www.webull.com/news/15687819044455424). Company guide (Q3 release 2026-06-25, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000038/cmc-5312026xearningsreleas.htm): core EBITDA up sequentially from $353.6m. NA Steel is up from the absent $20m outage plus a similar volume/margin benefit, CSG grows mid-teens and Europe ex-CO2 is modestly higher. Call summaries put the companywide uplift at +$40-50m (https://stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/CMC/2026/Q3). At about 111.6m diluted shares and a ~24% tax rate, the guide midpoint implies adjusted EPS of about $2.00-2.05, so consensus sits at or slightly below the guide midpoint. The Q3 base of $353.6m includes a $20.4m Europe CO2 credit, and whether the +$40-50m is measured on that base or ex-credit is ambiguous. That ambiguity is the main uncertainty in the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest is 6.3M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 5.2 days to cover, about 5.7% of shares outstanding. That is up from 4.7M / 3.6 days on 2026-07-15 and 6.2M / 6.5 days on 2026-09-15 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest/, read 2026-10-14). Shorts are building but the name is not crowded. In the baseline, the 25-delta skew is +27.2 vol points (downside paid). It is computed on a front expiry with total open interest of only 495 contracts, an ATM spread of 62% of mid and a put/call OI ratio of 0.39 (call-heavy), so the skew is a thin-chain artefact as much as a directional statement. The event-implied move is 4.98%, indicative only. Run-up: +3.1% over 5 days, -0.9% over 20 days, 21.6% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: Steel Dynamics' Q3 2026 guidance (Jul-Sep, issued 2026-09-17, after CMC last spoke on 06-25) says steel profitability is 'significantly higher' sequentially on 'metal margin expansion across the platform and record shipments', with 'average realized steel selling values to increase in combination with lower scrap costs'. It says demand is 'led by non-residential construction' and its fabrication backlog is 'nearly 50 percent higher than prior-year' and extends 'through the first quarter of 2027'. That is two months of overlap with CMC's FQ4 (Jun-Aug) and a direct read on the Sep-Nov quarter CMC will guide on 10-15. The market's expectation for CMC's FQ1 FY27 is the seasonal pattern: last year's Q1 guide was 'generally consistent' with Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-driven prints: 2025-10-16 (Q4 FY25, Q1 guided 'consistent with Q4' plus the debt-funded Foley acquisition announced) -7.26%. 2026-06-25 (Q3, guided a stronger Q4) +3.94%. A Stock Track item describes a -5.14% intraday drop on a weak Q2 EBITDA outlook (https://www.itiger.com/news/1120498183, date not verified).
findings.why_not_priced: STLD is mostly flat-rolled and was sold about 5% on guiding below consensus, so the market read the release as a steel negative, not as a long-products margin positive for CMC. CMC is still 21.6% below its 52-week high, only -0.9% over 20 days, and carries a positive put skew. If the read-through were priced, CMC would have re-rated after 09-17 and the chain would not be paying for downside.
findings.independence: Partly corroborated by US rebar holding about $1,022/t in August while scrap was flat (GMK 2026-09-17, https://gmk.center/en/news/key-global-markets-are-set-for-a-rise-in-rebar-prices/; SMU 2026-09-08, https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/09/08/smu-scrap-tags-for-shredded-hms-flat-while-busheling-ticks-up/), which is the next finding. That is a different source but the same margin mechanism, so the two overlap. This is a peer proxy: STLD's long-products share is a minority of its business.

findings.finding: US rebar averaged $1,022.3/t ex-works Midwest in August 2026 and 'remained largely stable', with mills avoiding across-the-board cuts (GMK, 2026-09-17). Scrap was flat: SMU September shredded $417.50/gt, unchanged from August, and busheling +$10 (2026-09-08); Fastmarkets has August down 0.8% m/m. CMC's FQ3 steel-products ASP was $989/ton and metal margin $610/ton. So the FQ4 (Jun-Aug) margin over scrap likely held or widened, which is inside the company's own guide of a stronger NA Steel quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats are not paid: Barchart counts four of the last five prints as day-0 declines despite some beats. Q4 FY25 beat consensus ($1.37 vs $1.34) and fell -7.26%. Q3 FY26 ($1.73, described as a beat or a slight miss depending on source) rose +3.94%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. This is the guided path and consensus EPS of about $1.97 sits at or near the guide midpoint. It is filed because it confirms the quarter will not miss on spread, which is the one way the reported line could surprise downward. If the market doubted the spread, consensus would sit below the company guide, and it does not.
findings.independence: SMU scrap (https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/09/08/smu-scrap-tags-for-shredded-hms-flat-while-busheling-ticks-up/) and Fastmarkets' September scrap outlook (https://www.fastmarkets.com/insights/us-scrap-trends-outlook-september-2026/) are independent of the rebar series. These are industry series, not CMC numbers.

findings.finding: Both large US steel peers guided their Jul-Sep quarter below sell-side consensus on 2026-09-17: Nucor $5.55-5.65 against a cited $5.99, and Steel Dynamics $5.34-5.38 against $5.60, after which STLD fell almost 5%. This is evidence that steel estimates this cycle are running ahead of what companies deliver. Nucor also flagged higher costs of products sold in its mills segment, which is the opposite of STLD's 'lower scrap costs'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CMC sells on guidance disappointments: -7.26% on 2025-10-16, -4.69% on 2026-03-26, -3.56% on 2026-01-08 (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: CMC's positive put skew and its 21.6% discount to the 52-week high may already carry this. What is not priced is that CMC's own consensus ($1.94-2.00, and about $2.00 on Benzinga) still sits at the top of the company's guided uplift, unlike peers whose consensus was cut on guidance day. CMC gives no mid-quarter update, so its bar was never reset.
findings.independence: STLD below-consensus guide: https://tradersunion.com/news/stocks/show/3390538-steel-dynamics-slides-4-74percent-to/ and https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/stld-gets-street-backing-despite-lower-than-estimated-q3-guidance-wells-fargo-remains-constructive-on-margin-upside/cZtHbViRBE2. Nucor consensus of $5.99 is from one German outlet only (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/nucor-aktie-fallt-nach-q3-prognose-gewinn-uber-vorjahr-aber-unter-erwartungen). This finding shares the 09-17 STLD document with finding 1 but reads a different element (guide vs consensus, not margin direction).

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 4.7M shares (2026-07-15, 3.6 days to cover) to 6.2M (09-15) and 6.3M (09-30, 5.2 days, about 5.7% of shares outstanding). Shorts are building into the print, but well short of crowded.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior squeeze on this name in the baseline. The largest move in seven prints is 7.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: The rise in short interest is public. The mechanism is that a 5-day-to-cover short base adds buying pressure if the Q1 guide holds up. At 5.7% that pressure is modest, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Benzinga's August snapshot had 5.1% of float with a declining trend (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CMC/sentiment), so the build is recent. No other source.

findings.finding: Polish domestic rebar was stagnant to softer through the summer. The Fastmarkets assessment, CPT Poland, was 2,650-2,700 zł/t in the week to 24 July 2026, down from 2,680-2,800 a week earlier, with the market described as 'stagnant; it's the holiday season'. Europe Steel was guided 'modestly higher ex-CO2' from a $14.3m ex-credit Q3 base. Europe is about 10% of segment EBITDA, so a miss here would be a few million dollars set against roughly $390-400m of core EBITDA, with the US and CSG making up the rest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the baseline traded on Europe alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Polish rebar is not followed by CMC's US-centred coverage. Netted against the 90% of EBITDA that is US and CSG, the effect is small.
findings.independence: none for August-September 2026. Earlier 2026: Cognor raised rebar about 20% from early 2026 (https://gmk.center/en/news/polish-company-cognor-has-raised-its-rebar-prices-by-20-since-the-beginning-of-the-year/), which points the other way on the level.

findings.finding: The EU's permanent steel import regime replaced the safeguard on 1 July 2026. Duty-free quota is cut 47% to 18.3Mt a year and out-of-quota imports pay 50% instead of 25%, with a melt-and-pour origin rule. That supports Europe Steel's FY27 outlook, which CMC will describe for the first time on 10-15.
findings.why_not_priced: The policy is public. What is unpriced is CMC's quantification of the effect on its Polish business, which it has not yet given. Europe is a small segment, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Council adoption on 2026-06-08 (https://gmk.center/en/news/the-eu-has-approved-new-safeguard-measures-on-steel-imports/). This is macro-to-company transmission that CMC has not confirmed.

findings.finding: At its 2026-08-05 Investor Day CMC added $600m of buyback authorization, taking the total available to about $717m, against a market cap of about $7.3bn at $65. The FQ4 (Jun-Aug) repurchase pace and any FY27 capital-return plan will be visible for the first time in the 10-15 release. FQ3 repurchases were only $18.9m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 repurchased $50.0m and the stock still fell -7.26% (the Foley deal dominated).
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is priced. The pace is not known: net leverage was 2.1x after the Foley and CP&P deals and management said it had visibility to below 2x, so whether it is buying back stock already is an open question.
findings.independence: Q3 release: $128.9m remaining before the increase and leverage commentary (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000038/cmc-5312026xearningsreleas.htm).

findings.finding: Europe CO2 credit timing is the swing item in reading the quarter. FY25 booked a $30.7m credit in Q4 and $15m in FQ1 FY26. FY26 booked $20.4m in FQ3, and the Q4 guide speaks of Europe 'excluding CO2 credits'. If no credit lands in FQ4, headline core EBITDA growth reads about $20m lower than a like-for-like reading. If a second tranche lands, it flatters the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 included the $30.7m credit; the stock fell -7.26% on other lines.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether consensus models a Q4 credit is unknowable from public estimates. The item is below the steel spread and has no path to the guide, so it is sized at zero with a band.
findings.independence: The FQ3 FY26 release records the $20.4m credit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000038/cmc-5312026xearningsreleas.htm).

findings.finding: The filings in the two days before the print are routine. The 8-K of 2026-10-13 declares the regular $0.20 dividend, unchanged after August's 11% raise. Form 4s dated 2026-10-12 to 10-14 are FY24-cycle PSU settlements with tax withholding at $63.89 plus new RSU grants, for example SVP Doucet: 5,887 PSU shares settled, 2,317 withheld, 9,598 RSUs granted. There are no open-market sales or purchases.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price. The filings are routine. The PSU payout percentage could reflect FY24-26 performance but is not shown as a percentage.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive, which is against the +27 vol-point put skew and against a name that has sold four of its last five prints. The skew sits on 495 contracts of open interest with a 62% ATM spread and a 0.39 put/call OI ratio, so it is a weak statement, but the reaction history is not. That is why p_up is held at 52 and not at the 55-58 the peer read-through alone would support.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (proxy vs company number): STLD's peer read-through cut from +0.8 to +0.6, because it is a mostly flat-rolled peer and CMC has not confirmed the transmission

Rules 1 and 6 (inside the guide; beats sold): the US rebar/scrap spread finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2, because it lands inside the company's guided sequential increase on a name that sold four of its last five prints
Rule 5 (proxy): the peers-below-consensus finding cut from -0.5 to -0.4. Short interest was checked before this negative: 5.7%, not crowded, so no further shrink for squeeze risk
Rule 7 (skew): p_up lowered from 53 to 52, because the leaning-positive sign runs against the +27 vol-point put skew, which is discounted for a thin chain but not ignored
Rule 2: the CO2 credit is filed as a one_off at 0 with no path to the guide. It was already at 0 in the draft
